# Browser behavior inventory

This is the working register for source-confirmed differences and missing browser
evidence. Add a row whenever an audit, capture or test discovers a difference.
Keep the browser version, primary source, implementation and remaining evidence
together. An implementation passing local tests does not establish full browser
parity. Close a row only for the explicitly recorded scope; retain capture and
platform limitations instead of silently treating them as a match.

Statuses: **in progress**, **implemented**, **open**, **unverified**.

For the reconciled implementation backlog and its separate evidence/scope
limits, see [Current remaining work](#current-remaining-work-2026-11-15).

All browser constants and cache policies belong in Surf profiles. Existing
forks expose generic protocol mechanisms only. Public cache settings are available
through `Builder.SessionCache()` and its terminal `Set()`, matching the other
Surf sub-builders. Profiles configure the same concrete fluent cache settings. Explicit application cache
choices take precedence over automatic browser-owned queues.

Go cache housekeeping is unrelated to this inventory: clear build caches only
when disk space is low. Do not delete downloaded module caches as routine cleanup.

## Verification for the ticket-cache implementation

The [session capture report](tests/testdata/wire/session_cache/README.md) records
new verified Surf ECH/resumption connections, an independent v1-to-v2/RTT
restoration peer and the exact scope of fresh native-browser observations.
Queue exhaustion, concurrency, rejection, custom ownership, protocol isolation
and nested-builder behavior are covered by deterministic regressions.

## Current Chromium revision

The [Chromium 158 audit](tests/testdata/wire/chrome_158/README.md) records the
primary source pins and independent native endpoint observations. Chromium is
the protocol reference; Surf keeps Chrome's User-Agent and Client Hints branding
for the selected OS.
The obsolete 157 public profile helpers are removed. Historical captures keep
their original version labels.

| ID | Scope | Expected behavior and current status | Evidence / follow-up |

## Header preset model

The unified model is implemented. Public SetHeaders/AddHeaders with g.MapOrd
remain the user API. Each browser's common/headers.go contains identity, defaults,
request scenarios, hint placement and protocol-specific positions. Platform
compatibility files delegate to it and hold no independent header policy.

BuildRequestHeaders returns a fresh ordered map. Its public HeaderContext contains
the request, selected OS, actual protocol, Critical-CH stage and redirect state.
Request.Fetch()/Navigation() set a concrete request kind. It is preserved through
redirects even on HTTP origins where no Fetch Metadata is emitted.
Protocol zero identifies logical defaults; the final call receives actual HTTP
major 1, 2 or 3. HeaderCase separately supplies H1 spelling, without changing
values or order. Factories never read or replace a request body.

| Step | Change and required invariant |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Logical defaults | Apply missing defaults before request middleware and refresh generated values afterward. Track explicit setters separately, even when their value equals a generated default. Keep layout metadata out of the logical request. |
| 2. User ownership | Public g.MapOrd records the user's sequence without preset sorting. Each metadata key retains independent ownership. Empty and nil explicit metadata are preserved. |
| 3. Dynamic hints | Client Hints owns origin opt-ins, cookies, body replay and restart state. It supplies values and restart context to the factory without maintaining an order snapshot. Empty declaration slots never enable unavailable hints. |
| 4. Final composition | The existing protocol-preparation boundary applies the factory on a private attempt. H3 Alt-Used is available before composition. Fallback starts again from logical headers. |
| 5. Preset declarations | Navigation, Critical-CH, redirects and fetch share one browser file. No built-in encoded method names or per-method caches remain. Blink's pure hash mechanics are separate from header declarations. |
| 6. Public compatibility | Existing standalone helpers delegate to the same factory. Custom variants without BuildRequestHeaders retain the previous callback contract. Placeholder mobile data remains explicitly labeled. |

The shared wire sorters remain responsible for physical emission. Host and
Content-Length positions are independent of their computed values. Existing
HPACK/QPACK references remain unchanged; full field-list tests also cover all
seven ordinary methods, TRACE/CONNECT, explicit order, pseudo order, body framing,
redirects, fresh/warm/Critical hints and both Surf/Std APIs. CONNECT retains the
existing TCP-only routing guard; no new HTTP/3 CONNECT API is claimed.

Native references establish the recorded H1 scenarios. H2/H3 variants in the new
method matrix exercise documented protocol deltas through real local peers;
they do not establish new native timing or scheduling parity. Current native
mobile, arbitrary renderer insertion histories and complete document context
remain separate evidence gaps.

| ID | Area | Status | Evidence / remaining scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ACK-LOOP-01 | Chrome ACK threshold under a full receive queue | **Implemented.** A policy-selected queued ACK reaches the send loop before the next UDP datagram. Native batching remains the engine default; Chrome enables AckFlushOnPacket and Firefox disables it. Baseline Linux captures move Surf from a late ACK median/max of 14/41 to 10/10, matching the native Chrome observation. | [Linux report](tests/testdata/wire/linux_load/README.md); queue, wakeup and ACK-reset regressions in the engine. Socket backpressure can still postpone a send; observed counts under loss are not pure trigger thresholds. |
| ACK-SPACE-01 | Firefox ACK probes and packet-number snapshots | **Implemented.** Policy snapshots read the selected number-space history, including shared 0-RTT/1-RTT data, rather than an unused shared history when separate spaces are enabled. Actual Firefox-profile PING probes return in the Linux captures. | [Linux report](tests/testdata/wire/linux_load/README.md); engine tests cover removed packets and path probes in both numbering modes. Exact PING counts remain dependent on RTT, outstanding packets and input batching. |
| RACE-POOL-01 | An older TCP winner after QUIC confirmation | **Implemented.** New requests reconsider a completed TCP decision once a usable QUIC connection is confirmed, including a decision retained in the other early/full-handshake slot. Existing waiters and pending shared preparations keep their ownership. | [Deterministic retained-winner regression](internal/connrace/race_test.go), [real TCP/UDP regression](tests/http3_connection_racing_test.go). Both are repeated on Linux; this does not establish browser first-use H3 eligibility/history. |
| WIRE-COLD-01 | Cold Firefox H3 on an impaired public path | **Reply-delivery boundary narrowed; exact cause unresolved.** Independently matched peer qlogs received the complete ClientHello and prepared Initial/Handshake replies in all three historical failures; the client captured no return UDP. Fresh native/Surf baseline, loss and reorder runs pass payload and ordered-header checks. Earlier failures remain failures and do not establish a client encoding/parser bug. | [Original evidence and fresh captures](tests/testdata/wire/cold_http3_path/README.md). Peer qlog preparation is not wire delivery; the precise queue/path/server-processing loss or delay point is not established. |


## Fixed desktop audit, 2026-11-14

The [24-scenario audit](BROWSER_AUDIT.md) keeps full-row `match`, `different` and
`unverified` evidence separate. Its four implementation phases add HTTP/1 write
policies, terminal HTTP/2 close policies, source-based HTTP/2 upload reads/DATA
caps, and owned TCP keepalive/HTTP2 idle-probe policies. Browser values remain
in Surf profiles; HTTP engine extensions are generic and documented upstream.

| Area | Verified result | Explicit limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTTP/1 writes | 56 current independent full request/record matches; mandatory streaming/Expect flush and body ownership regressions | Timed native arbitrary producer streams remain unverified |
| HTTP/2 close | 24 current native connection comparisons; normal/peer/error code, last-stream ID and exact tested debug data match; bounded/no-duplicate close | Every possible decoder diagnostic is not claimed |
| HTTP/2 upload | 64 current native DATA/END_STREAM and normalized TLS body-record vectors match; credit exhaustion/reset and streaming short reads tested | Arbitrary producer/socket scheduling is not a constant packet vector |
| TCP keepalive | Current 700-second native/Surf H1 and final 130-second H2 captures; real macOS/Linux socket-option and override tests | Host timer rounding/slack and Windows native kernel behavior are separate limits |

Evidence, capture hashes, source references and exact comparison boundaries are
in the [desktop report](tests/testdata/wire/desktop_audit/README.md). Public custom
settings are demonstrated in the [write policies example](examples/http/write_policies/write_policies.go).


## Current codec and paced producer follow-up, 2026-11-15

Fresh ordinary Chromium 158.0.8127.18 / Firefox 160.0 captures replace the
historical-only evidence gap for HPACK and QPACK. The [current sequence
report](tests/testdata/wire/desktop_sequences/README.md) retains all native inputs,
actual capture hashes, decoder limitations and the exact QPACK preparation
history. It confirms 22 HPACK field sections (eleven per browser),
96 complete QPACK field sections and eight encoder instruction streams under
the documented laboratory history. Historical native vectors remain labeled.

Paced unknown-length POST found and fixed Chrome's HTTP/2 fresh-read budget:
short reads must not shrink the next 16375-byte allowance. The HTTP engine adds
generic `RequestBodyOptions.MaxReadSize`; Firefox's persistent buffer/cycle
semantics and explicit overrides stay available. Three Chromium H2 DATA/EOF/TLS
projections and three H3 DATA/FIN plans now match native captures after this fix.
Both profiles have cancellation/ownership regressions across H1/H2/H3. A new
regression also fixed an HTTP/1 cancellation deadlock: the error path must close
the application reader before waiting for its blocked writer goroutine. Known
and unknown lengths are checked under cancellation, timeout and peer close.
Untouched bodies retain safe stale-connection retries without unnecessary
factory reopening. No-keepalive HTTP/2 admission also retires unused concurrent
TLS handoffs, preserving active streams and reservations. Retirement probe
registration now precedes the asynchronous ACK wait, preventing a duplicate
PING when a joining goroutine is delayed past the original acknowledgement.

Firefox Stable's unsupported ReadableStream request body and Chromium's H1
streaming Fetch rejection are recorded rather than bypassed. Go reader APIs
remain functional. DOM cancellation EOF followed by reset is distinguished from
Go context cancellation without a successful producer EOF. Arbitrary producer,
network and kernel scheduling remain outside exact packet equality.

## Current remaining work, 2026-11-15

Reconciled against Surf `262d385`, HTTP v1.0.47, QUIC v1.0.35 and uTLS v1.0.9.
This is an inventory, not authorization to implement every optional scope below.
The fixed desktop audit's four implementation phases are complete. In
particular, TCP-WRITE-01, TLS-RECORD-02, H2-CLOSE-01 and TCP-IDLE-01 must not be
reported as absent implementations; their old open labels were stale.
Historical maintenance plans and earlier capture reports retain their original
stage boundaries. Use current code and this register to decide what remains.

The complete browser job controller remains CHROME-NET-01 below. |

No additional repository fork is intrinsically required to investigate these
items: they concern Surf and the existing HTTP/QUIC/uTLS forks. The exact patch
size and browser policy still need review before any implementation promise.

### Open optional scopes and architectural limits

- **CACHE-02:** persisted browser-style network/ticket state is absent. Runtime
  cache compression and shared Firefox TCP/QUIC budgeting are implemented;
  compression is not disk persistence. Persistence is outside the fixed desktop
  audit and must not be enabled implicitly.
- **MOBILE-02 / IOS-01:** Firefox Android/iOS still have explicit 148 placeholder
  variants. Chrome iOS's existing template lacks TCP session resumption in the
  current tests. Complete native mobile/WebKit TLS/H2/H3 behavior needs its own
  references. Chrome Android is wired, but native mobile parity is unverified.
- **WEBTRANSPORT-01 / WebSocket:** there is no complete WebTransport session API
  or Surf-owned WebSocket frame/compression engine and builder. Surf's 101/Std
  interoperability and advertised H3 settings are separate existing features.
  These application protocols were not implemented by the desktop audit.
- **HINTS-02 / browser context:** DOM meta Accept-CH, frame Permissions-Policy,
  delegation, renderer resource ordering and a browser HTTP cache are outside
  Surf's current transport/document model. Application-provided values and
  partitions do not construct that missing context automatically.
- **CACHE-01 / TLS-CHAIN-01:** NSS and Go store different token representations,
  so identical compressed byte charges/eviction boundaries are not guaranteed.
  Go root verification with supplied intermediates also is not the complete
  Chrome Root Store, CT, pinning or revocation policy. These are explicit engine
  boundaries, not simple missing numeric profile settings.

### Implemented behavior still lacking complete native evidence

- **D03 / D16:** selected ECH retry/rejection, unknown-ticket, HRR and
  accepted-early-data/changed-SETTINGS native cases. The new
  [controlled peer](tests/tools/browserpeer/README.md) proves local controls;
  ordinary native trust/DNS/routing prerequisites remain unverified.
- **D04 / D14 / D15:** complete current native ticket-expiry/pressure, v1/v2
  negotiation and ACK/PTO/copy-retirement matrices. Existing mechanisms and
  scoped sources/interop/capture references are retained.
- **D11-D13 / D17-D19:** arbitrary producer/credit schedules, complete race and
  coalescing/privacy/error histories, and equivalent native proxy-route cases.
  Do not turn missing native evidence into a claim that the whole implementation
  is absent, or promise equality for every OS/producer scheduling history.
- **D24:** the original Firefox cold-path reply loss remains unlocalized.
  Complete ClientHello reception and reply preparation are established, as are
  successful fresh native/Surf runs. No client defect has been demonstrated.
- Native Android/iOS and Windows kernel behavior are separate from the desktop
  Linux captures or a Windows User-Agent identity overlay.

Prioritize bounded existing-desktop gaps before optional application protocols,
mobile placeholders or constructing a full browser scheduler/renderer. Reuse
the retained capture inventory; no new test or capture batch is implied by this
documentation reconciliation.
